evidence.note: Cleanly separated pipeline stages up front: built score.py (parser+scorer) as shared infrastructure, then a greedy baseline aligner, then optimizers — a real parse→score→align→optimize decomposition.

Both thresholds treated as explicit milestones and broken into derived numeric sub-targets (e.g. required Ea/E2 to reach S3=0.55); recognized DM-HS (S3 only) as easier than yeast (S3+NC), showing awareness of the two-deliverable asymmetry.

Instead of a single generic reusable aligner, wrote ~20 near-duplicate one-off scripts (opt3, targeted_opt, aggressor, robust_opt, grid_search, final_sa, etc.), i.e. failed to factor shared aligner infrastructure from per-instance tuning — the duplicated effort the task structure warned against.

Despite repeatedly noting DM-HS was the easier bar, it deferred that deliverable to the very end and produced only a broken S3=0.010 result; the two-deliverable sequencing was recognized but not executed deliberately.
Final submission with y2kr-SC S3=0.396 and DM-HS S3=0.010 confirms decomposition never resolved into a working per-deliverable milestone completion despite the stated stage structure.

reasoning: The agent clearly cleared anchor 5: distinct parse/score/align/optimize/write stages with both numeric thresholds treated as explicit per-deliverable milestones, plus repeated derivation of numeric sub-targets. But it stops short of anchor 8: it never factored a generic reusable aligner (instead rewriting ~20 duplicate scripts, only the scorer was shared) and it recognized but mismanaged the DM-HS-vs-yeast sequencing, neglecting the easier deliverable until it failed. That places the observed behavior between 5 and 8, at a 6.
